To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

exhaust plumes emitted ahead can affect on-road measurements of air pollutants, and that the extent to which the plumes affect the measurements depends on the distance between the vehicles, the vehicle speeds, and the background concentrations of the pollutants.

the overestimation of onroad air quality surveying measurements caused by exhaust plume from vehicles ahead of a mobile laboratory (in the case of a sport utility vehicle, SUV, as emitter vehicle) is significant when the vehicle ahead is a bus or sedan, but not when it is a SUV or sedan.
the overestimation of onroad air quality surveying measured with a mobile lab caused by exhaust plume of vehicle ahead in dense traffice areas is investigated by experiment and CFD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the unintended influence of the exhaust plumes of vehicles ahead on on-road air quality measurement.
the effect of exhaust plume on the on-road air quality measurements.
the unintended influence of vehicle exhaust plumes on the on-road air quality measurement by ML.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the influence of the exhaust plumes emitted by vehicles ahead of a ML is not negligible in dense traffic areas and the influence is dependent upon vehicle types and vehicle speeds.

the unintended influence of the exhaust plumes emitted by the vehicle ahead to the on-road air quality data measured with a ML at 20-30 km h-1 in the dense traffic areas is significant and should be considered.

the unintended influence of plumes emitted from the vehicle ahead to on-board air quality surveying is inevitable in dense traffic areas, and that the overestimation is dependent on the distance between the ML and the emitter vehicle, vehicle type, vehicle speed, background air quality, and height of the ML inlets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the overestimation of air pollution data measured with the ML in urban dense traffic areas is caused by the exhaust plumes from the vehicle ahead, and the extent of overestimation is dependent on the distance between the vehicles, background concentrations of the air pollutants, and the vehicle speed.

the unintended influence of vehicle exhaust plumes emitted ahead to on-road mobile measurement of air quality in dense traffic areas should be considered when the vehicle speed is higher than 20 kmh-1 and the distance between the ML and the emitter vehicle ahead is less than 40

a mobile laboratory should be operated at least 10 m behind the leading vehicle in dense traffic areas to avoid the unintended overestimation of air quality data caused by exhaust plume from a vehicle ahead.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the unintended influence of the plumes of vehicles ahead on the measurement data should be considered when the on-road air quality is evaluated by a ML.
the unintended influence of the exhaust plumes from the vehicle ahead of the ML should be considered in dense urban traffic conditions.
the influence of exhaust plume from the vehicle ahead of the ML should be considered in on-road air quality measurement in urban dense-traffic conditions.
